ai.title: Add sonnet 3.7 to message cost tracker
ai.summary: Added `models.sonnet3_7` to `TOKENS_COST_PER_M` in `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts` for `input`, `output`, `cache_creation`, and `cache_read`. Rates match existing `models.sonnet` entries ($3/$15/$3.75/$0.3 per M tokens). Internal cost tracking update; no user-facing changes.

eli5.text: The system now records how much it costs to use a newer version of one of its AI models in its internal ledger, using the same pricing as the previous version. Nothing about your experience changes, no new features appear, no buttons move, and no answers get better or worse. If you dug into the books, you'd see this new model listed alongside the others so accounting can track its usage at the same dollar rates as the model it replaces, but since that's the only difference, you wouldn't notice it at all.

ai.title: Refine endturn prompting for GPT-4.1
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to explicitly instruct GPT-4.1 to end turn immediately after simple responses. This adjustment aims to improve turn termination reliability for concise outputs while maintaining the requirement to complete all parts of multi-part requests. Scope limited to internal prompt logic for `isGPT4_1`.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that helps build responses was taught a small new habit: when it has a simple answer, it can now wrap up and signal for a reply sooner instead of keeping you waiting. This only applies to the newer internal model used for straightforward, one-part questions, and it doesn't change how complex, multi-step requests are handled. If you chat with the internal tools today, you may simply get a quicker handoff after short replies rather than a long pause.

ai.title: Expand few-shot examples in checkTerminalCommand
ai.summary: Added explicit 'yes' and 'no' few-shot examples to the LLM prompt in `backend/src/check-terminal-command.ts`. This aims to reduce false positives where natural language inputs are misclassified as executable terminal commands. The change affects the `checkTerminalCommand` function's prompt construction logic.

eli5.text: The assistant that decides whether something you type is a real command (like 'git pull') versus plain text (like asking to install something) now gets clearer examples of what counts as each. It shows more sample phrases, including cases where people type 'yes' or 'no' as part of a sentence, so it's less likely to mistake natural language for something you'd run in a terminal. This improves accuracy for internal testing on April 15, 2025, without changing behavior for live users yet. It's already in place in the codebase but only used during testing.

ai.title: Disable checkpoints in home directory
ai.summary: CheckpointManager throws CheckpointsDisabledError when getProjectRoot() equals os.homedir(). Prevents checkpoint creation in user home directories. Internal change in npm-app/src/checkpoints/checkpoint-manager.ts.

eli5.text: When someone tries to save a checkpoint while their project is sitting right in their home directory, the system now refuses and tells them it won't save checkpoints in the home directory. This only affects people who happen to be working directly out of their home folder, which is an unusual setup. If you tried it, you'd see an error message saying checkpoints are disabled in the home directory instead of a file getting saved there.

ai.title: Support absolute paths and tilde expansion in cd command
ai.summary: Terminal utility now handles absolute paths and tilde expansion for cd commands. Previously, relative path joining logic caused errors when users provided absolute paths or ~ shortcuts. The change introduces conditional checks for ~, ~/ prefix, and absolute paths before setting the project root. Also updates a comment in checkpoint-manager.ts to reflect correct worker script path.

eli5.text: When you tell the assistant to change folders by typing a full path (like /Users/yourname/projects) or use your home folder shortcut (like ~ or ~/Documents), it used to get confused and fail. Now it recognizes those inputs and goes to the right place, so you can switch to any directory on your computer just the way you'd type it in a regular terminal. This fix is live today and only affects people using the assistant's built-in terminal.

ai.title: Reset bare repo path on project root change
ai.summary: CheckpointManager.clearCheckpoints now accepts resetBareRepoPath flag. setProjectRoot passes true when switching directories, clearing stale bareRepoPath references. Prevents checkpoint corruption from lingering repo paths during directory changes.

eli5.text: When you switch to a different project folder, the assistant now clears out any old folder-path reference it was holding onto from your previous project. Without this, it could accidentally save progress markers pointing at a location you had already left, which could corrupt its ability to undo steps correctly. You wouldn't see anything new during normal use, but if you've ever switched folders and gotten confused undo behavior, that situation is now avoided at the moment you change directories.

ai.title: Rename Best Practices title
ai.summary: Changed frontmatter title in `web/src/content/tips/best-practices.mdx` from 'Best Practices' to 'Codebuff Best Practices'. Aligns doc metadata with sidebar section navigation fix. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: The internal documentation section that lists tips and best practices for Codebuff now has its heading correctly set to 'Codebuff Best Practices' instead of just 'Best Practices'. This small fix improves the sidebar navigation experience, making it easier for users to find and scroll through the relevant best practices content.

ai.title: Home dir project tree disables file listing
ai.summary: getProjectFileTree in common/src/project-file-tree.ts sets maxFiles to 0 when projectRoot matches os.homedir(), preventing any file enumeration. This blocks reading permissioned files in the home directory (#110). The change applies to shared core logic used by CLI and Web surfaces. Previously, the limit was 1000 files.

eli5.text: When the assistant's project lives in your home folder, it now shows you no file listing at all instead of the first thousand files. You will see an empty or collapsed folder view where the file count used to be. This applies to the shared project-view logic the assistant uses whether you chat on the web or via the command line.

ai.title: Skip checkpoint init in home dir
ai.summary: Added guard in initializeCheckpointFileManager to return early if projectDir matches os.homedir(). Prevents bare repo creation in home directory. Scope: npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts. Mechanism: direct string equality check against os.homedir().

eli5.text: If you try to start a new project from your home directory on your computer, the app will now skip setting up its behind-the-scenes tracking system rather than creating a hidden project folder right there. The app simply stops early when it realizes it's running in your home directory, so nothing gets created. This only affects what happens when you launch the app from inside that specific folder; starting projects from any other location still works as before. The behavior is live today for anyone using the app from its installed location.

ai.title: Version 1.0.218
ai.summary: Freebuff npm package `codebuff` bumped to 1.0.218. Change isolated to `npm-app/package.json` version field. No functional code or dependency updates.

eli5.text: The software was updated to a new version label. This is a routine behind-the-scenes update that keeps the installation current without changing any features or behavior. If you looked, you would see only the version number changed in the project's settings file.

ai.title: Rename browseraction tool to browserlogs
ai.summary: Renamed `browser_action` to `browser_logs` across backend prompts, common schemas, and CLI handlers. This clarifies the tool's purpose for retrieving console logs and errors. Updates include `main-prompt.ts`, `tools.ts`, `browser-actions.ts`, `constants/tools.ts`, `tool-handlers.ts`, and `tool-renderers.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to open a website to check for error messages or logs on the page, the tool label changed from 'browser_action' to 'browser_logs'. Anyone using this website-checking feature will see the new name in tool listings and prompts. The change only renames the tool; it does not add new capabilities or alter how the website checking works. The renaming is live today across all supported environments.

ai.title: Add intro text when starting in home directory
ai.summary: The CLI greeting now detects if `getProjectRoot()` matches `os.homedir()` and displays specific onboarding instructions before returning early. This prevents users from seeing confusing git-related errors when launching Freebuff without a project context. The change is isolated to `npm-app/src/menu.ts`.

eli5.text: When you launch the assistant from your home directory, it now shows a short message telling you to navigate to a project folder and ask for a code change, instead of showing confusing git-related errors. This only happens when your current folder is your home directory, and it affects anyone starting a session from there.

ai.summary: Package version updated to 1.0.219 in npm-app/package.json. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: If you updated the assistant today, you'd get a few small improvements that make it behave better: when it starts up in your home directory it now greets you with a short explanation, and the part of the assistant that works with your web browser now logs useful debugging info under a clearer name. These changes only take effect once you're running the latest version.

ai.title: Update referral instructions to include cd command
ai.summary: Referral page instructions updated to prepend 'cd /my/project/dir' to the 'codebuff' command. This ensures users navigate to their project directory before running the CLI. Change isolated to web/src/app/referrals/[code]/page.tsx.

eli5.text: When you click through a referral link on the website, the box that copies the installation command now includes a step to switch into your project folder before running the command. Previously the copied text read 'codebuff'; it now reads 'cd /my/project/dir && codebuff', so running the pasted command automatically moves you into the correct directory first. This only affects people following the on-screen referral instructions; if you run codebuff manually today, nothing else has changed.

ai.title: Store referral code in localStorage on unauthenticated visit
ai.summary: The `web/src/app/referrals/[code]/page.tsx` file now persists the referral `code` to `localStorage` under the key `codebuff_referral_code` when the user is `unauthenticated`. This ensures the code survives navigation or refreshes before login. The change is scoped to the web referrals page.

eli5.text: When someone who isn't logged in visits a referral page, the site now saves the referral code in your browser's memory so it stays there even if you click around, refresh the page, or leave and come back later before signing up. Only visitors without an account are affected by this.

ai.title: Move checkpoint handlers into cli-handlers/checkpoint.ts
ai.summary: Refactor: CLI checkpoint logic (`handleUndo`, `handleRedo`, command regexes) extracted from `npm-app/src/cli.ts` into new file `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/checkpoint.ts`. `cli.ts` now imports these handlers and the `checkpointManager` directly. `freshPrompt` in `cli.ts` updated to accept optional `userInput`, clearing and rewriting the readline line state to support restored checkpoint prompts.

eli5.text: The internal code that manages the assistant's undo, redo, and checkpoint listing commands has been moved into its own dedicated file, so the main startup file is now shorter and easier to follow. Anyone maintaining the tool sees the change immediately: the command logic they used to find in one large file now lives in a clearly labeled section, and importing it behaves the same as before. No new features or options are introduced; the assistant's ability to rewind or list conversations works exactly as it did today.

ai.title: Add checkpoint menu and save command
ai.summary: Added interactive checkpoint menu and explicit save command to CLI. Refactored checkpoint command handling in cli.ts to use centralized checkpointCommands object and isCheckpointCommand helper. Updated CheckpointManager.addCheckpoint to accept saveWithNoChanges flag, allowing checkpoint creation even when no file changes are staged. Covers npm-app checkpoint-manager.ts, cli-handlers/checkpoint.ts, and cli.ts.

eli5.text: You can now save a snapshot of your work at any time by typing 'checkpoint' in the conversation, even if you haven't made any file changes since the last save. The assistant also shows an interactive menu when you type 'checkpoint list', letting you pick which saved state to jump back to or clear all saved points. This only affects people using the checkpoint feature directly in the command line; casual users who don't type these commands won't notice anything different.

ai.title: Extract CLI handlers to dedicated modules
ai.summary: Refactored `npm-app/src/cli.ts` by moving `detectApiKey`, `handleDiff`, and `showEasterEgg` into new files under `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/`. Updated `CheckpointManager` logic to correctly handle `saveWithNoChanges` flag during checkpoint creation. Scope limited to internal CLI structure; no user-facing behavior changes.

eli5.text: The team split up one large internal command file into smaller, focused files that each handle a specific job - one for checking API keys, one for showing code changes, and one for the hidden easter egg feature. This is purely behind-the-scenes organization work; everything still works exactly the same for anyone using the tool. The only noticeable fix is that the checkpoint system now correctly saves snapshots even when there are no changes to save, which prevents it from unnecessarily creating checkpoints when it shouldn't. Nothing the reader would see or do has changed.

ai.title: Add git commit guide to system prompt
ai.summary: New `gitCommitGuidePrompt` constant added to `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts`, detailing a four-step workflow for creating commits. The guide mandates reviewing diffs and logs, analyzing changes in `<commit_analysis>` tags, and using a specific HEREDOC format with a `Co-Authored-By: Codebuff` footer. This prompt is injected into the `run_terminal_command` tool description in `backend/src/tools.ts`. Constraints include forbidding git config changes, pushes, and interactive flags.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to make a new git commit, it now follows a fixed step-by-step routine: it first shows you the pending changes and last few commit messages, then it summarizes what changed and why before running a commit command that ends with a quiet confirmation instead of opening an editor. You won’t see any of this text, but any commit the assistant attempts from now on will be shaped by those steps.
